clue.text: Hide constant desire

parts.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant (as the speed of light) in science
to ache for something is to desire it, so ache works as a noun for longing

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceal a lasting longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, and the noun is also a hiding place, so it stands for hide as a noun (a hunter's hide).

clue.text: Coach briefly played with Leeds United

indicators.note: played says the letters are worked over into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of coach goes

explanation.surface: A football coach had a short stint managing Leeds United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leeds United' reads as the club, but 'United' is the definition; 'briefly' gives COAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalesced means came together into one mass, so united.

clue.text: Lord, soldier and best friend of royalty

parts.note: Cor! is an exclamation of surprise like Lord!
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A peer and a soldier are the monarch's closest companions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Corgi is a Welsh dog breed famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: The late Queen kept corgis all her life, and a dog is called man's best friend.

clue.text: Person who doesn't want company to issue shares before

indicators.note: shares here means takes into its space, so the word for issue goes inside

parts.note: ere is a literary word for before
to emit is to issue or send out

explanation.surface: A recluse firm wants to release stock early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' and 'shares' suggest business; 'shares' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a recluse living apart for religious reasons.

clue.text: Paying back value of property mainly controlled by cartel

indicators.note: controlled by puts the trimmed value inside the cartel, which holds it

parts.note: a ring is a group of traders combining to fix prices, a cartel

indicators.note: mainly says most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: equity is the value of a property beyond what is owed on it

explanation.surface: A property deal repaid under the control of a price-fixing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter; equity here is the owner's stake in a property net of the mortgage.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay or return a favour or injury, so requiting is repaying.

clue.text: Person who holds up gown worn by bishop before Queen

indicators.note: before sets the gown first, ahead of the queen
worn by places the bishop inside the gown, as a wearer is within

parts.note: a robe is a long gown
B is the chess notation for bishop
R, for Regina, means Queen

explanation.surface: A clergyman's attendant lifts the bishop's train ahead of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' suggests carrying a train but means armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is an armed robbery, so a person who holds up is a robber.

clue.text: Grill hunting expedition over decapitated animal

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above, earlier than the second

parts.note: a quest is a search, an expedition hunting for something

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A hunt ends with a beheaded beast, ready for the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grill' suggests cooking but means interrogate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them, to question them closely.

clue.text: Start of invasion deployed sniper fire

indicators.note: Start of picks the opening letter of invasion
deployed means arranged in position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: At the invasion's start a sniper opened fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' reads as shooting but is a verb meaning stir up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to inspire them, filling them with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Loving marriage vow is written in loveless language

parts.note: I do is what the bride and groom say

indicators.note: written in means set inside, so is goes within the shortened language
love in tennis is zero, the letter O, which is dropped

parts.note: lingo is slang for a language

explanation.surface: Wedding vows composed in a cold, unloving tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes O (love, zero in tennis) from LINGO, leaving LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolising someone is worshipping or adoring them, an intense form of loving.

clue.text: Place for putting inexperienced member of party

definitions.meaning: a golf ... is where one putts
a ... is a member of the ... Party

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the party is shown where to put things.
explanation.definitionFit: Green covers all three: the putting surface in golf, naivety, and the environmentalist party.

clue.text: American beer and most lager turns out to be rather pleasant

indicators.note: turns out says the drinks' letters come out in a new order
most of the word lager means its last letter is left off

explanation.surface: A US beer plus most of a lager proves a nice drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' cuts the lager to LAGE; 'turns out' rearranges BEER and LAGE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable describes something mildly enjoyable or nice, a gentle synonym rather than strong praise.

clue.text: Took one's time boarding

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and into something, so time goes inside

parts.note: sole means of only one person, belonging to one alone, so one's gives sole

explanation.surface: Someone dawdled, taking their time getting aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took one's time' reads as one phrase meaning dawdled; the definition is just 'Took'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole is the past tense of steal, and stealing is taking without permission.

clue.text: Journalist provided formality and structure

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is crossword shorthand for a journalist
provided that means if
ice is coldness of manner, stiff formality

explanation.surface: A reporter brought stiff manners and order to a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, a grand structure.

clue.text: Express disapproval about one item that's charged in lessons

definitions.note: tuition is uncountable teaching, standing for lessons collectively

indicators.note: about means going round, so the disapproval surrounds one

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
I is the Roman numeral one
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A tutor tuts about a single chargeable item on a lesson bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests billing, but it is electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, given in a course of lessons.

clue.text: Shut up nearest and dearest after losing second son

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped, second points at the later of two matching letters

parts.note: closest means most intimate, as family are
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Telling family to be quiet after one boy is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like 'be quiet' but means confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To closet someone is to shut them away in private, as in a closed room.

clue.text: Having expelled extremists, Conservatives support entering 'New Right' candidate in race?

indicators.note: extremists here are the outermost letters, which are thrown out

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: entering says the support goes inside the pair of letters

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Tories purge hardliners and back a fresh right-wing candidate in an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests an election but is a cross-country running event.
explanation.definitionFit: An orienteer competes in races across country using map and compass, so is a competitor in one.

clue.text: He stops disparate voices coming together

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the pronoun sits inside the rearranged letters
disparate means scattered and unlike, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor halts a choir of mismatched voices so it blends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disparate' signals the anagram and 'stops' the insertion, the pronoun plugging a gap like a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesive describes parts that stick and unite, forming a whole.

clue.text: Watched as the author cried out loud

indicators.note: out loud says the words are spoken, giving the answer's sound

parts.note: the author is the setter, I, and cried is bawled

explanation.surface: The writer looked on, weeping noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaking of himself gives I BAWLED, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to stare at it, look at it closely.

clue.text: Said vegan perhaps could eat this

definitions.text: Said vegan perhaps could eat this

indicators.note: Said says the phrase is spoken to give the answer

parts.note: a vegan is an example of a veggie, and could is might

explanation.surface: A meat-free eater might enjoy this spread, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Vegemite is an Australian yeast-extract spread, suitable for vegans.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegemite is a plant-based yeast spread, so a vegan can eat it.

clue.text: Winger turned, ran and moved like this?

indicators.note: turned says the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: a bird is a creature with wings, so jokingly a winger
colours that ran are said to have bled

explanation.surface: A football winger turns and runs with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football but is a bird; 'turned' makes DRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer moving with the ball under close control is dribbling, which fits the football winger the surface pictures.

clue.text: Quietly say, 'Get clean clothes on!'

indicators.note: clothes means covers, so the cleaning word wraps round the other

parts.note: to bathe is to wash, get clean
re means about or on, as in on the subject of

explanation.surface: A whispered instruction to wash and dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb, enclosing RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe words is to say them very softly, almost a whisper.

clue.text: Highest point for one turning into adult writer

parts.note: A is the old film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: into puts the turned letters inside the adult and writer

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, American writer

indicators.note: turning says the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A writer reaches his peak when one turns grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EG to GE, which goes 'into' A + POE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the point of an orbit farthest from Earth, hence the peak or climax of anything.

clue.text: Led experimental programme on education

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a pilot is a trial run or test episode

explanation.surface: Someone headed a trial scheme in schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or guide, so piloted means led.

clue.text: Most peculiar aspect of childhood destiny

indicators.note: aspect of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Musing on the strangest part of one's fate as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd means strange, so the superlative is the most strange.

clue.text: This grant, in part, could be seen as accident-prone

indicators.note: could be seen as says rearranged letters of this answer and in part make up accident-prone

parts.note: the full set of letters to rearrange
these words supply letters that join the answer in the mix

explanation.surface: A grant, partly, might look like it's prone to accidents.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: this answer plus IN PART, 'could be seen as' rearranged, gives ACCIDENT PRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to grant or admit a point, as in conceding an argument.

clue.text: Named detectives charged with case of torture

indicators.note: charged with means filled with, so the detectives hold the letters

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

indicators.note: case of takes the outer letters, the shell of torture

explanation.surface: Police named and accused over a torture case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged with' suggests a criminal charge but means loaded with.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to name or mention, as in citing a source.

clue.text: (T)horny problem?

parts.note: a thorny problem is a hard one, and a choice between two bad options is said to have horns

explanation.surface: A tricky issue, with a cheeky bracket hinting at something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Without the bracketed T it is a horny problem: one is impaled on the horns of this.
explanation.definitionFit: One is caught on the horns of a dilemma, a difficult choice between two undesirable options.

clue.text: Filthy cold caught in this country, also caught by many on vacation

indicators.note: caught by places the result inside the emptied word
on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters
caught in puts the cold inside the country

parts.note: UK, the setter's own country
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in Britain catch a nasty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties MANY to MY, which holds U(C)K.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucky means covered in muck, dirty.

clue.text: Speaker leaking head of state's post on social media

indicators.note: leaking means losing contents, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a tweeter is a small loudspeaker for high notes
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen, Britain's head of state

explanation.surface: A spokesperson leaks the president's online message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests a person, but it is a hi-fi tweeter; ER, the Queen, leaks away.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short message posted on the platform formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: What, paradoxically, is spelt differently in dialect?

definitions.text: What, paradoxically, is spelt differently in dialect?

indicators.note: spelt differently means the letters are written in another order

explanation.surface: A riddle: which word, oddly, gets a new spelling in local speech?
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox: the word for 'same' is what you get by spelling IN DIALECT differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly the same, the opposite of differently, hence the paradox.

clue.text: Sad trend, getting drunk, encapsulates what finishes George Best

definitions.note: darnedest is a noun here, as in doing one's darnedest

indicators.note: encapsulates means encloses, so the final letter goes inside the rearranged ones
getting drunk means becoming confused, so the letters are rearranged
what finishes points at the closing letter of George

explanation.surface: The sad drinking of footballer George Best, who died of alcoholism.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer known for drinking; 'Best' is the definition, as in 'did his best'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing your darnedest is an informal idiom for doing your utmost, your very best.

clue.text: Wood spirit is something used to promote Prohibition?

parts.note: a dry area or era bans alcohol, as Prohibition did
an ad, an advertisement, promotes things

explanation.surface: Asking whether a ghostly drink is a campaign for temperance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood spirit' sounds like alcohol, fitting Prohibition, but is a nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth, a spirit living in woodland.
